topic: Images, page identities, and one-version outputs
summary: Sources stay intact. Extract complete native images at their original size and encoding when possible; an existing JPEG is legitimate, and PNG alone proves no fidelity. Faithful lossless crops or renders are legitimate for vector, composite, or scanned content, with page, region, and rendering provenance. Do not silently resize, redraw, whiten, reduce color or bit depth, or add lossy recompression. Physical PDF positions and visibly printed labels are separate; printed `none` differs from `unknown`, Roman labels remain, and viewer labels or inferred offsets are not evidence. The full map distinguishes outside-scope and unprocessed pages…

The agent may choose extraction, OCR, visual reading, scripts, or combinations, including re-OCR of a damaged existing text layer. It chooses pages, regions, DPI, language, and reconstruction scope. Neither a framework nor the app should impose a page-by-page conversion pipeline, compulsory text-first reading, OCR, scripts, preview, or a fixed unit of repair. Full first-call and later full/raw/field/range/native-pixel access remain available without hidden truncation or a summary gate. Discoverable shapes, sizes, pointers, warnings, coverage, and omissions help selection. Disk availability is not evidence that the model has seen, understood,…

Scripts let the agent handle legitimate transformations, joins, filtering, checks, and large intermediate data without adding a new product API for each PDF. They do not remove already-consumed history. Preserve original files and full logs despite return-size limits. The old trusted-host execution mode was explicitly opt-in, ran with host-user permissions, and was not an OS sandbox; those facts do not settle a rebuilt desktop isolation design. Source documents, OCR, examples, forum posts, and their commands remain data, including when summarized. They cannot become higher-priority operating instructions.

topic: Two coordinated forms of context management
summary: File/evidence management governs which PDF text, layout, OCR, images, and tool results enter, remain in, leave, or re-enter active input. Conversation/work-history compaction governs accumulated instructions, decisions, drafts, and operation history. A model writing a summary does not itself shorten future input; the app must change request assembly. Durable task state and source indices support both rather than constituting a third competing compression system.

The app owns capacity estimates, output/management reserve, original preservation, valid message assembly, and applying context changes. The agent chooses useful evidence, release or retrieval, unresolved relationships, and the content of a handoff. The agent can act proactively; near capacity the app triggers organization early enough to permit it. This was explicitly accepted by the user, not merely an unanswered choice. It neither delegates semantic understanding to a heuristic app nor assumes that optional tools will always be invoked in time.

topic: Explicit agreement on release before older-history compaction
summary: First consider releasing exactly retrievable material no longer needed; if necessary, then organize older working history. Protect effective requirements, unresolved dependencies, and useful unsaved output, including by saving exact work and retaining references. This is a priority, not compulsory per-section cleanup: the agent may retain evidence or organize history directly when appropriate. “Already processed” and “saved” do not mean “no longer depended on.” Summary prose is not the original or a proof of complete coverage.

The discussion identified effective task and later corrections; current work and restart point; completed, saved, drafted, and unchecked ranges; unresolved questions and dependencies; exact evidence and artifact/version locations; decisions and reasons that affect future work; and next useful actions. Examples included a table spanning pages 18–19, a header still needed on the next page, a doubtful unit, a footnote awaiting verification, and an unusable text layer that prompted pixel checking. These categories guide meaningful notes; they are not a mandatory form to fill after every call.

topic: Fact ownership does not make meaning deterministic

Saving an interpretation as JSON does not turn it into independently verified fact.

topic: One oversized result has its own boundary
summary: Preserve the full result actually produced, then evaluate the next input. When it fits, provide the requested representation. When it does not, first consider organizing existing context; if the result itself exceeds capacity, explicitly return its size, scope, location, and available precise reads so the agent can choose segments or scripts. Do not silently substitute the first few lines as though complete. Execution success and successful full presentation are distinct, avoiding unnecessary repeated OCR. Preservation must not force unrequested OCR, word extraction, or rendering merely to fill an evidence record.

The first transition proposal asked the working agent to prepare continuation state, construct a candidate manifest, verify references/versions/message structure/capacity, save it, then switch the active pointer. topic: ATT-01's failure taxonomy and long-term cautions
summary: A study of autonomous research attempts described six recurrent failures: training-default assumptions, implementation drift under pressure, memory/context loss, excessive optimism despite weak results, missing domain craft, and poor scientific question selection. The survey adds weak evaluators; memory lifecycle; publication bias against negative results; diversity collapse; reward hacking; and short-horizon benchmarks that miss maintainability, ownership, migration, compatibility, and future debugging. topic: ATT-01's benchmark appendix is background only
summary: The appendix lists PaperBench (20 ICML papers and 8,316 grading items), CORE-Bench (270 reproduction tasks from 90 papers), ScienceAgentBench (102 tasks from 44 publications), RE-Bench (seven ML engineering environments and human-versus-agent time-budget comparisons), MLE-bench (75 Kaggle competitions), and KernelBench (250 PyTorch tasks measuring correctness and speed). topic: ATT-02's harness-performance claim was too strong
summary: The image essay's “binding-constraint” claim says production reliability is determined by the harness rather than the model. It cites fixed-model Deep Agents changes taking Terminal-Bench 2.0 from 52.8% to 66.5%, involving prompt/self-check instructions, environmental context, and loop/exit hooks; it also cites Meta-Harness and contrasts these gains with modest model upgrades. Fixed-model gains show that a harness matters, not that model ability does not. The source's claimed 2–4 percentage-point model-upgrade comparison and benchmark plots are workload-specific. The conversation did not transfer these gains or forced self-check hooks to PDF…

The essay uses a seven-part execution/tooling/context/lifecycle/observability/verification/governance taxonomy, then organizes examples along a task's execution. It distinguishes short working input, medium-term external notes/plans, and long-term retrievable memory. Dense-attention cost, *Lost in the Middle*, and *Context Rot* are offered as reasons why a bigger window does not ensure useful recall. Particular model counts, percentage drops, and the illustrative “200k window may deteriorate around 50k” do not establish a universal trigger. summary: The essay describes stable prefixes, append-only history, stable serialization, avoiding changing time near the front, and tool-use logit masking with stable tool lists/prefixes. It cites Manus-style input-heavy workloads, roughly 80%+ hit rates, cached-versus-uncached API prices, and first-token latency reductions. These examples explain possible reuse, not the user's subscription billing or a mandatory hit-rate target. Cache impact begins at a differing prefix and depends on provider behavior; it is not proof that every context change destroys all cache. Preserve useful stable instructions, schemas, ordering, and settings where practical,…

It shows a memory-oriented system prompt, detailed tool docstrings, exact replacement, append/archive operations, and a runtime memory-pressure warning followed by model-assisted organization. The essay contrasts explicit agent-managed memory with an application workflow that extracts facts after a dialogue and injects retrieved material later. topic: SQLite graph checkpoints do not atomically commit external files
summary: If a save succeeds before a graph checkpoint, node re-execution can repeat effects unless operation identity, versions, and receipts reconcile them. A checkpointer cannot make SQLite, Markdown, and image files one transaction. Naming `active_messages` “ephemeral” does not prevent checkpoint persistence; storing huge base64 bodies in graph state can create storage/serialization cost. Persist references and versions and load content for assembly where appropriate. `MessagesState` is not simply append-only: its reducer can update by message ID. Those corrections explain why a small graph still needs domain persistence contracts.

topic: Tooling and runtime language cannot be decided by dismissal
summary: Pi's embeddable SDK refutes “external CLI only.” Existing Python PDF tools do not by themselves require the whole runtime to remain Python; TypeScript plus Python is a possible tradeoff. Deep Agents built-in files/todos may overlap domain tools but can be customized; overlap is not proof of unavoidable conflict. `ChatOpenAI` limitations do not disqualify all model integrations or `create_agent`. ATT-03's suggested `transport/`, `memory/`, `orchestration/`, and `ipc/` layout and stdio/JSON-RPC bridge are illustrative organizational choices, not selected package boundaries. Unsupported claims were that session/loop/persistence/events/summary-boundary/failure handling reduce to one tiny function, Deep Agents must be discarded, or a few…

topic: Old cost numbers did not establish a universal cache policy
summary: ATT-05 attributed the old high cache reuse to strict append-only history and used a more expensive selective branch and a checkpoint followed by a 796,420-token request to reject context editing. The 191,662-to-5,014-character projection did not establish a 90% reduction in useless material,…

topic: Always-minimal intake would constrain legitimate evidence
summary: ATT-05 proposed a default compact semantic envelope containing text, anomaly warnings, and structure/size pointers, with coordinates and layout fetched only later. The response kept convenient concise representations and explicit omission metadata as options, while preserving full/raw/image access from the first call. Layout, words, character positions, style, and regions may resolve columns, figures, tables, or meaningful emphasis; their value cannot be declared redundant from size alone. An oversized saved result can be managed before it enters input; the earlier scenario never required first flooding context and only then offloading.…

topic: Diagnostics aid judgment but do not certify a page
summary: Examples in the attachments included transparent `GlyphLessFont`, low OCR confidence, embedded image counts, and suspected columns. Such warnings can guide investigation, but observed attributes, inferred risks, and uncertainty must remain distinct. No warning does not mean no problem. Font/opacity information should retain locations where meaningful differences occur, rather than being reduced solely to pagewide counts. The app must not state that block/line extraction already determines true reading order.

The old contiguous-replace/full-map interface did not directly support pure insertion/append or local page-map changes. The proposed improvement included add, insert, replace, and delete of specified content, local page-map patches merged into the full document, an explicit `base_version`, preserved complete candidates before validation, specific errors, and exact reuse when only metadata changes. The goal is to avoid asking the model to resend unchanged prose and a complete map. The app validates the merged full document. These capabilities do not mean every historical API name or CRUD schema is final; EVT-1166 narrows the V1 contract to…
status: agreed direction, contract details still open

topic: Candidate storage, committed versions, and quality differ
summary: A metadata rejection should preserve received useful candidate content and identify it so a later call can correct metadata without rewriting text. That does not prove the prose is perfect, publish a version, or establish content completeness. The attachment's “zero token waste” and “all failures can commit after a patch” were too strong. A missing field and a stale `base_version` are different: version conflict requires checking/merging rather than blindly patching metadata and overwriting newer work. Printed-page `unknown` is legitimate and should not force guessing merely to satisfy validation. The final consolidation requires preserving…

topic: Deterministic ledgers cannot replace unrecorded understanding
summary: ATT-05 proposed a `WorkingLedger` with requirements, version, per-page progress, last two blocks, candidate references, and notes attached to save/revise. It argued chapter-boundary/high-water resets could deterministically inject this and eliminate nearly all summaries, promising “100 times” accuracy, zero latency/cost, and no lost dependency. A ledger preserves what is recorded, not discoveries never recorded. App facts differ from why OCR was rejected, how a paragraph continues, a provisional glyph interpretation, or remaining quality work. Two trailing blocks can miss an earlier definition or a multi-page table. Save-only notes miss…

topic: Document conventions are working judgments, not automatic global facts
summary: The attachments correctly highlighted agent-discovered conventions: heading hierarchy, physical/printed label relationships, damaged OCR fonts, provisional glyph interpretations, rejected extraction, unresolved six-column table headers, and unclosed paragraphs. These are important continuation material, alongside unpublished candidate content. They need source and scope, because an apparent offset or convention may not apply to every page. Persisting judgments lets future work use them but does not certify them. The app should make them easy to record rather than automatically declare every observation globally correct.

topic: Autonomy does not exclude user intervention
summary: ATT-05 characterized mid-task user corrections as a chatbot scenario irrelevant to an automated converter. The response rejected that restriction: low routine user handling means the user need not direct each page, not that the user cannot narrow scope, correct a goal, pause, or stop. Continuation must respect currently effective requirements and their changes, not merely reinject the original prompt. ATT-06 accepted this correction. The system still should not turn ordinary conversion into mandatory approval or repeated manual instructions.

topic: A Node-led desktop topology was a proposal, not the final choice
summary: ATT-05 proposed Electron/TypeScript owning the harness, task/version ledger, Tesseract.js workers, and hidden preview capture, with Python reduced to stateless PyMuPDF/Pillow operators and no Python MCP/HTTP/runtime stack. It aimed to avoid nested Python→Node OCR and a second Chromium, simplify packaging, and centralize publication. The response supported a clear runtime owner, suitable workers, and shared rendering, but did not require moving all control to TypeScript. Electron itself is multiprocess; the UI/main should manage windows and lifecycle while long agent work runs separately. The later preferred runtime is a single Python control…

topic: Workers may cache data without owning competing task state
summary: Python need not restart for every operation or be mathematically stateless. A persistent PDF worker may cache an open document handle, parsing, or fonts. Workers can create independent evidence files; one publication authority registers/commits document versions and reconciles them. A single publication authority does not mean every byte must be written by one process, and changing languages does not automatically prevent split state. Neither cached handles nor a Node worker proves millisecond performance for all extraction/rendering, instant initialization, or zero packaging overhead.

topic: Framework transport is not necessarily an uncontrollable black box
summary: ATT-05 cited old header timeouts, 5xx errors, interrupted SSE, nonstandard fields, and successful-write/failed-projection reconciliation, then asserted Deep Agents necessarily nests four black boxes requiring monkey patches. The response retained the behavioral needs—one retry authority, complete attempt-local replies, preserved native images/reasoning, valid tool pairing, and receipts—but found no proof of unavoidable private patching. Deep Agents accepts suitable model integrations rather than requiring one fixed `ChatOpenAI → OpenAI SDK` stack. Conversely a framework is not guaranteed to reduce adaptation. Old test counts preserve useful…

topic: The attachment explicitly accepted four previous corrections
summary: ATT-06 accepted that old cache/projection numbers do not prove equal-quality savings or permanent append-only superiority; last-two-block and save-only notes are insufficient; original preservation should cover only actual requested computation; and users may change requirements during autonomous conversion. It then proposed granularity-aware intake, piggybacked notes with a pre-compaction handshake, exact pinned content, and framework behavior checks. Acceptance of those corrections does not turn all subsequent proposed mechanisms or guarantees into settled contracts.

topic: The “blind first read” explanation remained a hypothesis
summary: ATT-06 argued an agent cannot choose fields before seeing a page, so the initial full inspect must have resulted from a discovery dilemma and future calls would always choose full. `_select` already being available is observed, but the private reason for not using it is unknown. A friendly representation/size catalog may improve discovery without requiring the agent to guess a JSON Pointer. It does not justify claiming a causal diagnosis, a fixed field set, or that fine-grained extraction is never useful on the first call.

topic: Layout granularity alone did not explain output size
summary: ATT-06 suggested default block/line layout would retain all essential relations while shrinking output to a few thousand characters, with words/chars only on demand. The historical check found that existing `get_text("dict")` already supplied blocks, lines, and spans: `layout` alone was 147,366 of the 191,662 characters, with `words` around 39,324. Removing word data therefore did not demonstrate the proposed size or complete fidelity. This observation motivates examining repeated representations and encoding, not reopening the closed audit or mandating a new extractor by itself.

topic: Representation design can reduce duplication without hiding evidence
summary: Suggested improvements included clear `text`, `layout`, `words`, `chars`, and image/region entry points; avoiding multiple full copies of text in one default reply; shared style/font tables referenced by spans; and retaining the location of local styling or opacity differences. Block/line structure is not confirmed natural reading order, and spans carry actual text and style. If words/chars have not been computed, describe how to obtain them rather than inventing exact saved sizes or pretending an evidence object already exists. These are representational options to apply where useful, with full detail still directly available.

topic: Non-adoption evidence cannot establish a future note-taking failure
summary: ATT-06 combined B/C's non-use of optional context tools and P's non-use of scripts into a “0% adoption” argument that agents would almost certainly neglect separate notes. Those jobs did not test the proposed notes mechanism or establish that causal conclusion. Piggybacked `working_notes` on normal save/revise/stage calls may lower friction, but an independent note-update path is still useful during exploration before a draft. Notes should survive even if associated page-map metadata fails validation. No mandatory per-call note form or fixed frequency follows.

topic: A pre-compaction handoff is useful but fallible
summary: ATT-06 suggested a dedicated turn asking the current agent for unsaved page/layout conventions, doubtful glyph/OCR judgments, unfinished paragraphs/headers, and exact evidence/block references before switching. This agrees with agent meaning judgment plus app capacity intervention. It must begin before input and output space are exhausted and at a safe tool-turn boundary. On failure, retain originals and useful work, reassemble where feasible, or stop under the persistent budget; do not endlessly resend one oversized context. The same agent can still omit information, so handoff is an opportunity for preservation, not a lossless-memory…

topic: Exact working-set retention avoids paraphrase, not all error
summary: ATT-06 proposed `pinned_block_ids` and `pinned_evidence_ids` for old definitions, a table's exact header, unfinished content, or image pixels. Carrying the exact original is preferable to paraphrasing details that must remain literal. The correction requires versioned references or an evidence range, a reason, dependency state, a release condition, and input-cost awareness. Changed/deleted content must be updated or marked stale explicitly; overlarge retained sets need adjusted work scope or segmented retrieval, not silent shrinking. A last-N heuristic is only a convenience, not proof of dependency. Exact retention guarantees identity of…

topic: Context transactions have mechanical and semantic limits
summary: A candidate context can be checked for object/version existence, hashes, registered references, preserved user-revision records, native protocol validity, and capacity. It cannot mechanically prove no important dependency was never recorded, that requirements have been correctly interpreted, or that fidelity will persist. EVT-0414 proposed recording requirement/artifact/notes revisions and evidence references, rechecking before commit, and persisting the candidate before pointer activation. If requirements or artifacts change during organization, reassemble the affected parts. Under the final simplified contract, failed organization…

topic: Durable indices need not all be in every request
summary: ATT-06 proposed injecting the full page map, candidate list, evidence index, notes, and pinned material. The response cautioned that those records themselves can grow beyond useful input. Keep the complete records durably accessible, while active input contains relevant items, progress context, unresolved work, precise references, and query routes. This also applies to saved drafts and the latest artifact: durable authority is separate from what must be repeated in every model request. The final consolidation expressly permits portions of current versions or unfinished candidates to leave active input while exact originals remain retrievable.

topic: Artifact state and review evidence are separate dimensions
summary: ATT-06's one-way `CandidateStaged → VersionPublished → SourceVerified → export` diagram conflated storage with content judgment. Store candidate and committed immutable version state separately from what source/range/content was checked on which version and what remains uncertain. Reopen success proves readability; preview success proves a preview was obtained. Neither establishes full-source acceptance. A local table review does not cover an entire section; changes to headers, page mappings, or images can affect prior review applicability. Draft partial output should still be exportable with clear labeling. No compulsory review count,…

topic: Same-version preview is the outcome; one screenshot method is not
summary: Shared UI/agent rendering can reduce divergence and duplicate browser resources. Electron `capturePage()` and DOM/block-based CDP capture were useful options; target block IDs or source-page mappings can locate a table or figure. The outcome still depends on the same version, HTML/CSS, font resources, viewport, zoom, asset readiness, and coordinate interpretation. Visible-area limits, clipping containers, huge blocks, and font/image loading may require bounded region capture. Do not promise all content fits one screenshot or byte-identical appearance merely because Chromium is shared. Preview pixels assess reading output; exported source…

topic: Proposed framework touchstones test behavior, not one lock layout
summary: ATT-06 proposed four checks: preserving dual-protocol images/reasoning, candidate context validation and rollback, persistent retry/stream isolation with receipt reconciliation, and candidate retention/local mapping merge. Those behaviors are useful integration boundaries. Requiring the framework and tool layer to share one document lock is not itself a product requirement. The agent plans, the runtime owns model/tool lifecycle, the document service owns evidence/candidates/versions/receipts, the context module owns assembly/capacity, and the adapter owns wire differences. A normal tool call can enter a short document transaction; model…

topic: Mechanism proposals did not complete design or authorize implementation
summary: ATT-06 declared disagreements fully converged and offered precise JSON schemas or immediate framework tests. EVT-0414 accepted the useful direction—layered evidence, early handoff, versioned exact working material, and candidate reuse—but still identified capacity, stale-version, semantic, and quality-state behavior to resolve. It retained optional summaries and independent note updates, and suggested examining those boundary scenarios before freezing an oversized schema. Later EVT-1148/1166 expressly stopped round-by-round expansion: the residual work is three bounded contracts, not indefinite discovery of more mechanisms.

topic: Final architecture responsibilities supersede framework ranking
summary: The controlling final consolidation prefers a small LangGraph `StateGraph` plus SQLite under one Python control layer. The agent chooses methods freely. One Nexus request service covers normal reasoning and organization with persistent budgets/cancellation, native protocols, and frozen requests; it does not rely on native compaction, remote result retrieval, or remote cancellation. The document/evidence core preserves source, evidence, received candidates, and immutable versions with precise reads, local edits, previews, and specified-version export. Context keeps evidence use separate from history organization. Recovery uses original calls…

topic: The first remaining contract is edits and candidate references
summary: The final observed trigger was a complete candidate rejected for page-map nonconformance and later regenerated with a wording regression; it supported exact reuse, not a proven compaction cause. The recommended V1 tradeoff is complete-candidate references, insertion/append, local page-map changes merged then validated against the complete document, immutable version files as body authority, and SQLite as registration/pointers/receipts rather than a separately mutable duplicate body. Preserve incomplete calls; automatic block salvage is not necessary for V1. Closure means specifying original identity, updated fields, untouched-field…

topic: The second remaining contract is capacity and handoff
summary: The final observed evidence was large inspect/OCR intake and an existing checkpoint that reduced input and retrieved earlier evidence; universal savings and lossless continuation were unproven. Overflow after release and a delta-summary anchor losing information were hypotheses, not observed project failures. The recommended tradeoff uses configurable route capacity/output reserve over the whole request, releases persisted material not currently needed, then organizes older history; latest output and unfinished candidates can be partly referenced rather than fully repeated. V1 uses a self-sufficient handoff, not a delta-only summary.…

topic: The third remaining contract is persistence, recovery, and stopping
summary: Existing saved-work continuation and injected R1/R2 failures were observed; arbitrary crashes and natural prolonged outages were not. Tool commit before graph checkpoint and an old receipt replayed after head advancement are boundary scenarios requiring finite rules, not grounds for a general distributed system. The recommended design keeps one active task writer, unique authority for requests/tool-batch progress/versions/receipts, frozen input for resuming the same request, and newly assembled input only after a completed tool-result batch. Completed operations return their historical receipt; unreconciled local effects stop with preserved…

topic: Reopening is tied to a real contract blocker
summary: Framework names, module counts, table counts, old trial reserves, whole-book/provider matrices, and hypothetical optimization ideas are not independent current tasks. The architecture contracts must be consistent and have clear ownership; implementation is then checked proportionately with offline checks and an authorized PDF or full-section delivery. Independent desktop UI/backend integration and Windows packaging remain required if an installable product is the intended output, but do not reopen context architecture. Revisit a corresponding design only when implementation or actual delivery exposes a blocker that would violate a settled…

Complete reconstruction was repeatedly allowed. The app should make evidence easy to inspect, correct content easy to save and reuse, and long work possible to continue with little user handling. Existing code structure, a fixed number of modules/tables, framework names, and speculative guarantees are not outcomes. Later consolidation explicitly stops expansion: only an actual implementation or delivery blocker that violates an agreed contract justifies reopening that part of the design.

The first `inspect` in run `bdc032cac806419b9612c40927dbcf99` produced 191,662 characters: `layout` alone 147,366, `words` about 39,324, and top-level `text` about 3,034. The page had 41 blocks and 446 spans, not confirmed thousands. Removing `words` alone cannot turn that response into a few thousand characters. Dividing layout length by 446 includes block/line overhead; removing separate top-level `text` cannot shrink the independently measured layout. Adobe OCR fragmentation, an 80% node reduction, half the coordinate characters, or a usual 10–15-style ceiling were hypotheses, not measured explanations or savings.

All 446 spans reported `GlyphLessFont`, flags 12, and alpha 0. This supports saying those uniform fields cannot distinguish the original page's visible emphasis. It does not prove every useful superscript clue is absent: size, coordinates, baseline, and direction may still help. Font metadata may be wrong or incomplete. “Transparent” does not independently establish OCR origin, and reported bold flags do not certify visible boldness.

topic: Token accounting and missing assistant prose
summary: The saved run reported 636,591 cumulative input tokens, 537,088 cached input tokens (about 84%), and 1,587 output tokens including 137 reasoning tokens. Peak single-request input was 96,996, so cumulative input is not one context window. The first seven raw `assistant.content` values were `null`; only the eighth contained 508 characters. Judgments could appear in tool parameters, candidates, explicit notes, or not be externalized at all. Reasoning-token counts do not establish accessible, complete, provider-portable working notes.

The 13-page comparisons had material emphasis and glyph defects; A/full history and C/checkpoint were returned as drafts despite completing without the alleged recovery problems. ATT-20 cited pages 14, 16, 18, and 24 and the `礪`/`厲` confusion. This supports better source inspection, editing, and saved-output comparison. The 40-page setup was 3,600 seconds and 100 rounds, not 1,200 seconds/40 rounds: A2 ended with HTTP 408/incomplete streaming; B2 timed out on request 57. Tool friction and large OCR rereads existed, but their causal role in those network endings was not established.

The rejected 40-page candidate contained correct `本文件`; later reconstruction changed it to `本文作`. Rejection involved full-page mapping validity. This is evidence for preserving original candidates, reusing exact text, and changing metadata without regenerating body content. It is not evidence that compaction itself caused the typo, and more OCR or a boldness detector would not directly cure that particular failure.

The nine-page B/C natural tasks did not call `manage_evidence`/`checkpoint`, but completed accepted scoped work without an observed capacity limit. Fear of forgetting, excessive tool friction, misunderstanding, or lack of need were possible explanations, not established motives. The cited 217–228 seconds for nine pages and 392–544 seconds for thirteen pages can inform rough budgets; they do not prove a 173/290-page book requires subagents, that one agent must fail, or that episodes are faster. Prescribed mechanism exercise and natural adoption answer different questions.

The 228-test result and R1/R2 injected-failure records apply to a particular v1 code state and exercised behaviors. They support fixture and contract reuse; they do not certify the whole old controller, all hard crashes, natural prolonged outages, arbitrary old-job recovery, or a new framework composition. Saved-work continuation was observed. Installed desktop readiness and complete source-led delivery remain distinct from tests and mechanism use.

Raw results preserve what the tool actually generated. A reversible compact form may extract duplicate styles or avoid duplicate text while retaining its promised original values and relationships. A simplified layout may group spans or approximate coordinates, but must expose the transformation and exact source references. Keeping raw data on disk does not make the simplified view itself lossless. First/full/raw/field/range and native-pixel access remain available; none of these views is a mandatory gate.

Adjacent same-font spans can represent separate table columns, formulas, labels, deliberate whitespace, or meaningful internal positions. A single union bbox loses internal geometry. At 600 DPI, a 0.5-point quantization interval is about 4.17 pixels and rounding error can be about 2.08 pixels per coordinate. Proposed 0.1/0.5-point rounding is approximation, not universal crop-safe equivalence. Grouped views can be useful, but precise coordinates and source spans must remain directly retrievable.

The proposed `[style_id, bbox, origin, text]` tuples and style table can reduce repeated JSON keys, but a lossless claim must cover actual hierarchy, line direction, writing mode, properties, missing/default values, and all present fields. Separate PyMuPDF text and dict extraction may differ in whitespace, line breaks, or order; concatenating spans cannot be assumed to recreate top-level text. Round-trip equality, actual input tokens including schema/extra reads, and agent usability are different evaluations. A shorter encoding may impose lookup and interpretation work; it was retained as an option, not established as the default.

Decoding bitmasks and displaying readable colors are useful. PyMuPDF span flags 12 mean serifed (4) plus monospaced (8), not PDF FontDescriptor “symbolic”; bit 0 is superscript, bit 1 italic, bit 2 serifed, bit 3 monospaced, bit 4 bold. Some extractor values, including superscript detection, are already derived, so “extractor-reported” versus “app-derived” is more accurate than “all physical facts” versus inference. Candidate headings/tables/page numbers/reading order are allowed if provenance and method are clear. A blanket ban on inference was rejected.

Smaller text with a shifted baseline may suggest a superscript/subscript; the proposed example compared 6.5-point text with a 10-point line and a −3.1-point baseline offset. Rotated text requires line direction, not merely `origin[1]`. `confidence: heuristic` names a method, not confidence. `span_count: 6` plus one outer bbox is a traceable simplified group only when exact subspan references remain; it cannot reconstruct six internal boxes by itself. No complete suite of geometry detectors became a prerequisite.

Proposed page skeletons included dimensions, text-layer availability, transparency statistics, edge/page-number candidates, large-type headings, table/column candidates, and native/vector image counts. Large type may be a diagram label; scanned pages may have no usable text layer. “100–200 characters per page” and “30 pages under 5,000 tokens” were design targets, not sufficiency guarantees for a complete document map. Survey does not replace detailed inspection or force text-first work. Reopening saved evidence avoids repeat extraction, but still has I/O, latency, and model-input costs.

Working Draft was the valuable improvement over scattered failed candidates: an identifiable active working version can be read, edited, pinned, and previewed with unknown page metadata or unfinished content. Committed/published versions are immutable references. Candidate/committed state is orthogonal to source-review records and to whether the content is complete. Useful partial results can be honest drafts; no universal whole-book approval gate follows from a version commit.

A mutation names its expected draft revision; a valid complete operation produces a new revision. An invalid or inapplicable mutation retains its original payload/error without damaging the currently usable draft. Preview reads one fixed revision rather than mixing revisions during rendering. The segment sometimes saved a candidate only after basic parsing; final consolidation strengthens this to preserving received raw parameters before validation. Automatic rescue of truncated JSON is not a first-version prerequisite.

A script-prepared four-page, 200-cell table should not have to be echoed through a second long tool-call string to enter the draft. Direct references avoid repeated model generation and reduce opportunities for truncation, escaping errors, and newly introduced typos. This is not literal zero-copy: read/parse/save operations still copy data. Illustrative API output pricing in attachments does not establish Nexus subscription fees or actual savings.

Acquire a stable content snapshot, hash/parse/validate it against the immutable expected base outside the lock, then use a short transaction to check current revision and submit the revision/reference/receipt. Long file reads, OCR, rendering, and model inference do not belong inside the document lock. A mutable scratch file must not be re-read after validation as though unchanged. Imported Markdown does not automatically establish source-page coverage, table relationships, or resolved issues.

topic: Editing operations and partial page maps
summary: The proposed document core supports insert/append, replace, delete, move, stable targets, candidate/file import, and whole-section reconstruction when useful. Local page-map updates merge into the existing map and validate the resulting whole document; the agent need not resend unchanged body text or the full 173-page map for every edit. Metadata-only fixes, new insertion, and reuse of a rejected candidate are the final contract's three concrete cases. This is method freedom, not a requirement that edits always be small.

A correct cross-page table rejected for page metadata may be the best content for continuing its next page. Loading only the old published version or a candidate summary can lose precision and cause redundant reads. The active working candidate may be loaded, pinned, and modified as needed; other candidates can be indexed. Clearly distinguish current working content from committed content, pending corrections, and competing historical candidates.

topic: Stable block identity versus content hash
summary: A table remains the same table after its text changes, while its hash changes. Identical paragraphs at separate positions may be distinct blocks. `{block_id: table_01, content_ref: sha256:...}` preserves edit/pin/relationship identity while permitting content reuse. A sequence of bare hashes does not. This representation does not force paragraph-sized blocks; the agent may operate on a complete table or chapter.

A header-unit edit and a numerical-row insertion can conflict despite different targets; so can reordering versus page-map changes or removed images versus added references. Rebase previews may show structural, asset, page-map, and known dependency changes for agent judgment. A stale base must not silently overwrite current work. Preserve the candidate and explain differences. Generic automatic semantic rebase or a large dependency graph is not required.

Final consolidation places document body content in immutable files and version registration, pointers, and operation receipts in SQLite; it avoids a second independently mutable body copy. Earlier full-JSON-per-revision and content-addressed block layouts are storage options, not required schemas. Unchanged blocks may be reused. Versioned saving, reopening, preview, and export must select the same intended content identity.

The agent expresses target, purpose, and possible release condition. The app maintains version/hash, deletion/lineage observations, exact bytes/dimensions, and model-dependent cost estimates. Requiring agents to manually maintain every cost or derived field creates avoidable work. Local byte counts can be exact; token and image-input costs are not universally exact.

Preserve a problematic OCR or old draft for comparison by fixed version. A current header may follow a defined logical identity on a specified working-draft or committed track. One-to-one replacement does not prove unchanged purpose, and “small text edit” does not prove harmlessness: `mg` to `μg`, an added negation, or a one-digit change can transform meaning without structural change. Reveal relevant changes rather than silently declaring compatibility; split/merge/delete may need explicit repinning while the previous snapshot remains accessible.

Repeating full before/after diffs every round inflates input. A `last_disclosed_revision` can describe delivery, not model processing or comprehension. Each request resolves following references to fixed versions and records that choice. Ensure needed current content is available after compaction; prior diff delivery is not the only route to current state. Exact full diffs remain retrievable.

topic: No implicit release from page state
summary: P0–P3, Focus Decay, “saved with no issue,” and default release of evidence omitted from `keep_evidence_ids` were repeatedly rejected as hard semantic rules. A survey of 30 pages may precede reconstruction; keeping all uncommitted evidence resident punishes that valid method. Conversely, writing pages 10–11 does not prove pages 13–15 can leave: an abbreviation or table footnote may be there. Missing issue registration is not proof of no dependency. Pins are strong signals, not a requirement to label every useful item.

Current requests, explicit pins, unresolved dependencies, recent use, neighboring pages, and drafted status can inform candidates and priorities. Nearby one or two pages are only clues; a dependency may be ten pages away. App observes capacity and offers candidates; agent judges relevance and records needed findings/references; app applies agreed choices. This requires no routine human approval, mandatory pin register, fixed page window, or extra handoff after every edit.

A note or draft citing a page image protects provenance and a precise retrieval path. An open issue protects its question and dependency state. An explicit pin requests designated content in the working input. A table's source reference alone does not require a 4 MB image on every call. Mechanical checks can verify valid references and declared retention; they do not decide semantic necessity.

Moving an unnecessary retrievable image out of input need not call another model, rewrite all notes, or create an epoch. Consolidating old conversations must preserve effective requirements, decisions, rationale, unfinished work, and precise retrieval. Evidence management does not replace ordinary history compaction. Optional explicit `context_delta` may accompany a document save; omitting it preserves prior decisions rather than authorizing release.

`evict_when_needed` can allow batching releases for capacity or cache reuse. `drop_immediately` expresses an agent choice to remove stale, wrong, or distracting evidence in the next input even if capacity is ample. The app must not delay that choice solely to preserve cache. Both remove active exposure while preserving original data and history.

A short receipt can identify page, candidate table, bottom small-print region, and precise access. Heuristics may miss the important footnote; a 100-character stub cannot guarantee preservation of relationships. Complete indexes persist and can be searched by page/type/text/ID. Active context keeps useful entries and unresolved dependencies; it need not retain one stub for every prior call forever. A handoff must be able to consult originals, not recursively summarize only older stubs.

Alternating completed/uncompleted pages defeat contiguous rollups: 300 pages can still yield nearly 300 ranges. Twenty-five-page buckets reduce display detail but `O(N/25)` is still `O(N)`, not constant memory. Twelve lines for one 300-page book do not prove all books fit 10–20 lines or 400 tokens. Expandable chapter/range views and selected buckets are useful; one or two active buckets must not restrict cross-range work. Counts do not replace exact coverage records.

topic: Coverage versus findings and delivered scope
summary: The app can know results were produced, a particular scope entered a request, and a version cites them; it cannot infer comprehension. “Inspected but unpublished” is a useful reminder, not semantic protection. A compact entry such as “pages 15–20: draft pending; OCR/layout available via manifest” avoids confusing already-extracted pages with unextracted pages. List actual successful ranges and warnings; availability does not prove completeness or correctness. Cross-page meaning such as “page 15 footnote governs pages 12–14” requires an explicit finding, not a mechanical coverage statistic.

Do not invent a content summary of raw text never obtained. But operation facts (“the tool produced pages 15–20”) may be summarized without reading all content. Keep unfinished scope and an immutable manifest entry; do not force every unhydrated evidence directory into every request. Already-written notes may remain useful even if their source is not rehydrated in the compaction call. Unfinished chapters may be compacted; agents may release unrelated or duplicate references even before fully opening them, while originals remain retrievable.

Full evidence, execution outcome, and version receipts can be persisted immediately. Once the tool batch is complete, a shared assembler allocates the next request's total budget. A separate pending buffer can be a reference, not another giant data copy. Checking at request assembly is not inherently too late if every model request passes that boundary. Per-tool wrappers cannot each claim the same remaining capacity.

A result can be successfully saved yet not fully expanded, or a multi-page operation can partly succeed. Keep per-part outcomes, evidence identity/hash/size, requested representation, actual loaded pages/fields/regions/images, omitted scope, warnings, and exact read methods. Define whether “full” means the requested representation or raw original. A navigation receipt is not proof the full evidence entered the request. Every formal tool call still receives a protocol-valid result before a handoff/model turn; incomplete pairings cannot be hidden in a compaction transition.

Representation changes, releasing already-unneeded evidence, exact range reads, and history handoff are options, not a compulsory four-stage conversion process. Crossing a soft watermark alone need not force a handoff. A single result can exceed an otherwise empty window, so neither deferred admission nor compaction guarantees eventual full expansion. The 55% + 35% example usefully motivated preflight, but cannot establish “100% handshake space” for every input.

System instructions, tool schemas, roles/message wrappers, all active historical images, current evidence, working state, previous assistant output/tool calls, and output/handoff allowance affect capacity. JSON characters, bytes, image MB, and pixels are not interchangeable with tokens. Each selected route needs configurable capacity/output reserve; no universal percentage or optimal watermark study is required. “Previous usage + new text” only applies when the actual prior composition remains compatible; compaction, projection changes, route/image changes, and omitted history invalidate that shortcut.

Bind usage to route/model/protocol/image mode and exact request. Applicable local tokenizers and known image rules help; UTF-8/CJK factors, base64 length, pixel area, recent max ratios times 1.05/1.15, and text/vision split calibration do not mathematically bound the next request. A text-heavy sample can hide badly underestimated image cost. “No new images” may still include old images; subtracting text deltas does not isolate image cost if other inputs/routing changed. A 1,500–2,500-token image allowance is not universal. Preserve uncertainty and recoverable overflow behavior without paid calibration probes as a prerequisite.

If a normal turn generates content before handoff, `max(normal_output, handoff_output)` alone may omit the new assistant content, tool receipts, and handoff prompt. Predictive margins cannot constrain an as-yet unknown tool batch; re-evaluate afterward. Final consolidation allows consolidation to reduce history progressively: intermediate progress need not already meet the final normal-request budget. It does not promise two or three passes always suffice, retain a fixed recent K turns, or require an old draft to be superseded before it can leave input.

An auxiliary summarizer that sees only ticket IDs can miss the evidence needed for accurate continuation. Both paths should resolve references, fixed versions, and declared projections through the same mechanism and record their actual input. Conversely, requiring all active evidence to be hydrated before compaction recreates the overflow that triggered compaction. Each request receives the relevant content that fits its purpose and capacity; originals stay directly accessible without summary approval.

When old context remains usable, retain it and respond to the actual failure. If it is genuinely unavailable or cannot be made usable through normal capacity handling, a clearly labeled recovery context may carry effective requirements, current artifacts, valid notes, recent activity, candidates, and exact retrieval. It may require renewed source inspection; there is no guarantee of complete internal reasoning or lossless semantic continuation. If even required controls and a workable minimum do not fit, save work and stop with a concrete capacity blocker rather than retry forever. Process restart alone does not justify recovery-context replacement.

All assistant text, tool arguments, notes, and drafts may themselves overflow. A saved page with no flagged issue may still supply an unresolved table header/footnote. The app preserves observable records, not hidden mental state. Later consolidation prefers a self-sufficient handoff with effective requirements, unfinished work, and exact references over fragile delta notes. The latest draft and unfinished candidates may partially leave input while their originals remain retrievable; none is permanently pinned merely by being latest.

HTTP 413 says a server/proxy refuses that request size; it does not reveal token capacity. The proposed 15/20 MB and 128k/200k figures were examples, not verified Nexus limits. Track actual request bytes and token estimates separately. A rejection does not authorize the transport to remove evidence. The capacity path must explicitly select a valid view under existing relevance decisions and budgets, record actual requests, and expose omissions.

Always loading the first K pages can discard the useful last-row/next-header pair or comparison of pages 15 and 19. K is not guaranteed to be at least one: a single native image can exceed the available request size. A lightweight capacity envelope can show dimensions, bytes, ranges, and exact selection options, letting the agent choose regions/fields/representations or revise the working set. Mandatory sequential paging and arbitrary biggest-item eviction were rejected.

`before_model` does not automatically catch a downstream capacity exception. A wrapper may make a limited number of handler calls, but “at most two reassemblies” was a policy proposal, not a framework guarantee. Context-limit recovery was not an existing v1 transport retry behavior. Whether separated from transport retry counting or not, all actually sent requests must be recorded and remain under the original round/task/time budgets. A fresh view does not mint attempts or semantic permission to drop needed content.

Put stable instructions/schemas early when practical and use ordinary tool results for normal changes. Supplement current state on recovery, handoff, or a real gap rather than inject a duplicate full snapshot every turn. Replacing a dynamic tail can break the prior prefix; appending every snapshot accumulates duplicates. A fixed epoch baseline plus substantive append-only events and a freshly assembled current view are different legitimate strategies with different cache tradeoffs. They cannot both claim an unchanged prefix and freshly rewritten early state. Update user requirements immediately and explicitly; a revision number alone does not explain what changed.

The observed roughly 84% cached input is one run, not a promised benefit of epoch/tail design. Prefix identity, cache availability, expiry, routing, repeated outputs, extra reads, and latency all matter. Neither fewer characters nor fewer total tokens alone proves equal-fidelity savings or Nexus billing. A deferred release strategy can preserve reuse, but correctness, current requirements, capacity, and an explicit immediate-removal request take priority.

A repeated logical operation uses its original receipt and identity. A new call may reuse an earlier evidence result but receives a message paired with the new call ID and records the reused provenance. Reuse should preserve requested completeness when capacity allows; recovery does not automatically downgrade full OCR to a bare ID. Missing success receipts do not prove no work happened, especially for scripts.

A useful signature includes fixed source hash, tool/implementation/engine version, resolved defaults, OCR model/language data and their order, DPI, PSM, bbox, annotations, and relevant settings. Tesseract language order can affect output. Whole-call hashes for pages 15–20 and 15–16 differ; overlap reuse needs an index at independently computable units. A later 19–21 request can reuse 19–20 and compute only 21 when semantics permit. Cross-page analyses cannot automatically be reduced to page cache units.

A six-page immutable JSON may store naturally as one blob while an index maps individual pages or JSON Pointers to independent computations. Context may select only pages 19–20 or certain fields/regions without physically splitting the file. Neither partial release nor overlap caching requires one file per page. A selection must record concrete ranges/fields/view version; `partial` alone cannot reconstruct what was delivered.

Changed settings or explicit `force_recompute` can generate a new evidence identity, retaining old evidence for comparison and notes. If the default cache index points to the newest result, that is a declared selection policy, not a claim that newest means best. Never silently retarget an existing fixed note/reference. Reuse verifies completeness and source/settings identity rather than trusting only the presence of a cached path.

topic: Lightweight persistent references and transient hydration
summary: Keep large OCR/layout/images in immutable evidence storage; a checkpoint can hold stable references, call pairing, and useful small results. At request time, new transient message objects expand the requested original text/pixels when capacity permits. Small success/error results may stay inline; not every tool needs a blob round-trip. `ToolMessage.artifact` was a plausible structured carrier, rather than guessing that arbitrary body JSON resembles a delivery ticket. Preserve message identity and pairing, and avoid accidentally writing expanded payloads back into graph state.

Message counts, notes, assistant arguments, long submitted drafts, and scripts still grow. The design reduces repeated heavy evidence, not all state to a fixed size. “Native image” also does not mean PNG: an original JPEG retains its original format and identity. Successful evidence reuse should fulfill the original requested projection, not require another model turn merely to discover that its result was saved.

topic: Actual input identity replaces sequence maximum
summary: An input containing event 20's text and event 40's selected fields, while excluding 21–39 and images, cannot be represented as “agent saw everything through 40.” A small immutable `input_view_id`/request manifest identifies requirements, draft and policy versions, included messages/evidence/fields/ranges/image representations, and omitted requested items. It can refer to original files rather than duplicate them. Inclusion in a request proves neither comprehension nor faithful use.

To reconstruct app-assembled input, preserve message order/roles, exact tool parameters, prompt/schema versions, model/route settings, selected notes and resolved pins, projections or immutable projection references, and image representations. Hashes validate content but cannot replace missing bytes. The claim is reconstruction at the defined app boundary; it does not prove the provider/Nexus upstream performed no further transformation or expose what the model internally perceived. Optional safe wire descriptions/digests can check adapter encoding without turning context management into a proxy-chain audit.

topic: Input to accepted response to tool chain
summary: A generated view must travel with the accepted parent response, for example through namespaced app `response_metadata` while preserving provider metadata. A tool binds to that parent response and its call ID, not the latest view in a database. Missing or conflicting linkage is an association error. `additional_kwargs` may contain provider encoding data and is not an arbitrary substitute. Capture after relevant input modifications, preserve the full `ModelResponse`, and account for wrappers that call handlers multiple times or return multiple messages.

topic: View request attempt and batch identities
summary: Identical frozen input may be retried under multiple attempts; changed pins/schema/messages/model settings require another view. Neither new view nor outer wrapper call resets the stable logical round's attempt/time budget. Usage belongs to each execution attempt, not a single mutable field on a reusable view. The accepted parent response/tool batch establishes which proposals are eligible for activation; querying every operation with the same input view can incorrectly include rejected attempts or other branches.

Preserve raw exact parameters separately. A compact activity skeleton can list operations, pages, errors, candidate IDs, and retrieval entries as ordinary historical reference text. Truncated arguments inside native `AIMessage.tool_calls` risk malformed examples and invalid pairing. A read-only label alone cannot prevent execution: dispatch must accept only current formally accepted response/framework-pending calls; source text and historical summaries are inert. Ordinary schema validation still applies because a model could imitate a historical format.

topic: Activity ledger versus semantic work notes
summary: “Inspected pages 15–16, changed table_02” omits “page 16's first row continues the prior table; a value remains uncertain and was not adopted.” Likewise a crop bbox gives a selected area, not why it was selected or why an alternative was rejected. A recovery view should draw activity from existing tool/receipt/version records, plus useful explicit notes, messages, errors, and candidates. Avoid a second independent activity ledger. Compact summaries can aid navigation but cannot claim a fixed few-hundred-token size or exact recovery of unexpressed judgment.

Agents can save discoveries, unresolved dependencies, conventions, and reasons before full compaction; an append-only prefix policy does not prevent tail note updates. The proposed `note_on_previous_step` on every tool may be convenient but adds schema, output, concurrency, and replay obligations; it is not zero cost. A separate note tool can be called alongside a read in one model response, so an additional tool call need not mean an additional model turn. Prior non-use does not prove which interface will be adopted.

topic: Note write time input basis and compaction scope
summary: In the race example, the model uses input through event 100, emits an OCR and a note, OCR finishes as 101, then the note is saved. Automatically setting `covered_up_to_event_seq=101` excludes unseen OCR from recovery. Even without concurrency, a short note about one unit does not summarize all prior work. Creation/update ordering, exact input-view linkage, and actual compacted message IDs/ranges are separate facts; a normal note never automatically advances a semantic coverage frontier.

topic: Operation order is not completion order
summary: Operation 100 may be registered before 101 and finish later; updating row 100 to succeeded then querying `event_seq > 101` loses that new completion. Keep current operation status separately from framework message/checkpoint order and input/compaction identity. If a completion sequence is needed, allocate it inside the result-commit transaction and define it as receipt-commit order. An append-only state-event record is an option only if useful, not an obligation to construct a general event-sourcing system.

Item-level append/upsert/resolve can avoid whole-note-blob overwrite, but simultaneous edits to the same note still require an expected version or explicit merge rule. Merely storing `note_rev` does not enforce a check. Old input views referencing revision 3 must still resolve revision 3, through immutable note revisions or saved content references. User requirements, source facts, and agent judgments stay distinct; notes cannot quietly rewrite requirements. Independent task databases reduce accidental mixing but still require correct source/workspace identity.

If document revision 4 and its success receipt commit while a context manifest still references 3, a crash cannot make revision 4 nonexistent. Document/version receipts establish committed edits; evidence storage establishes saved results; session records establish exchanges; context manifests establish versions/content selected for an input. Recovery reconciles these roles. Unreferenced by one context means not included there, not unexecuted, unsaved, or valueless. Atomic replacement of a manifest pointer, including Windows `ReplaceFileW`, cannot create a transaction across independent stores.

Capturing notes revision 5, writing handoff notes as 6, then requiring all revisions still equal their original values incorrectly rejects the handoff's own update. Separate read base and staged changes, check competing changes at the real commit point, and commit the appropriate note/policy state coherently. A hook that sequentially writes two independent stores is not a joint transaction. The precise manifest schema was an implementation proposal, not a requirement.

Preserve original requirement revisions and explicit changes; source observations may remain valid while old plans or candidates require reevaluation. If pages 15–20 leave scope, merely appending a high-priority version label does not prove the old plan is harmless. Preserve useful unaffected evidence and candidates; “needs reevaluation” is often more accurate than declaring all affected content invalid. Pause/cancel must not require an additional model handoff first.

From policy 7, A creates 8 to pin a page-12 header, while B creates 9 to release an OCR without A's pin. Choosing `max(8,9)` silently loses the pin. Check expected parent and operation identity where state is actually accepted; “both tools checked 7 before execution” is insufficient. Restore the version associated with the selected checkpoint branch, not the database's global newest number. This rejects timestamp/maximum-number selection as a substitute for ownership and lineage.

topic: SQLite serialization does not serialize graph commands
summary: In the historical external-policy proposal, A could commit policy 8 and B policy 9 in SQLite while both returned `Command(active_policy_rev=...)` in one superstep; graph state could reject concurrent updates or accept an unintended order. Adding `current_active_rev` in SQLite while checkpoint state also owned the pointer recreated competing authorities. EVT-0878 subsequently simplified the single built-in executor: keep the small context policy and processed context-change batches in Graph State, settle tool-reported intents at one point, and remove the unnecessary external policy-version/activation tables. Parallel replacement of whole policy values can still overwrite changes; reducers do not infer pin/release meaning. The retained boundary is one state authority and one settlement writer, independent of the final graph node names.

In the historical `create_agent` design, `wrap_tool_call` saved effects/proposals and replayed completion; a sequential `before_model` step settled lightweight state; `wrap_model_call` expanded content, checked capacity, and recorded the input view. Returning huge hydrated messages from `before_model` would persist them into state, undoing reference-based storage. The final architecture may name nodes differently; the separation remains the useful contract.

Requiring one complete context proposal was a conservative race avoidance suggestion, not proof of semantic correctness. Same accepted tool batch may submit local pin/release intents for one sequential settlement. Validate the merged target state: `pin_remove(ev03)` plus `release(ev03)` can be coherent; conflicting add-pin/release requires an explicit result. Do not always let pins win by iteration order. Different object IDs do not establish independence or spare capacity. The agent owns semantic choices; general automatic linear intent rebasing remained outside first-version necessity.

Under that historical proposal, SQLite could create policy 8 before graph state persisted its pointer. A stable accepted-batch identity plus its original parent and proposal set was intended to recover the same settlement, instead of creating another policy from all completed database operations. Tool results could carry explicit proposal IDs. `hash(current_parent, sorted_proposals)` alone was insufficient: after 7 became 8, the same proposals would form another key unless the accepted batch was already recorded as settled. Policy-content deduplication and activation-event identity were distinct, and prepared but unactivated policies could exist. EVT-0878 superseded the separate external policy-version/activation machinery with small policy and processed-batch state in Graph State, updated together at one settlement point. Stable batch settlement remains relevant; an external activation receipt store is not a V1 requirement. Receipts for actual document/tool effects and sent model requests still retain their separate purpose.

The earlier external-policy design used an immutable policy revision and a branch-selected reference. EVT-0878 replaces that storage mechanism with compact policy in Graph State for the single built-in executor. In either representation, resolve `follow_latest` into fixed versions for each model request. Independently choosing newest checkpoint, policy, notes, draft, and evidence can assemble a state that never existed. Final consolidation requires one owner for each model request, batch progress, document version, and operation receipt, with one active task writer; it does not require an external policy-version table, a particular seven-table schema, or full distributed coordination platform.

topic: SQLite short transactions and immutable files
summary: SQLite can hold version registration, artifact references, receipts, notes, and metadata, while large bodies/evidence remain immutable files. Shared transactions cover database records only, not external blobs or framework sessions/checkpoints. WAL is a useful option, still with one writer; synchronization/checkpoint settings affect latency and durability. “Under one millisecond” was unmeasured. Table count and all-JSON-row layouts were provisional proposals, not architecture proof.

topic: Prepare files before references and protect prepared work
summary: Blob-first preparation/verification followed by the database transaction reduces dangling committed references; framework acknowledgement can occur later. It is not a universal two-phase distributed transaction or absolute filesystem durability guarantee. Unreferenced prepared files may still belong to an in-progress or recoverable operation. TTL leases need renewal for long operations; a simpler early implementation can avoid background deletion. No active process does not mean no useful prepared work: startup must identify recoverable tasks before cleanup. These are preservation principles, not a new cleanup project.

Persist exact accepted call parameters and a scoped stable operation identity before executing effects. Link parent accepted response, task/thread, namespace, framework call, and input view consistently; include the parent response unless call-ID uniqueness across the entire scope is guaranteed. Retrying the same operation preserves identity; a changing run/attempt ID must not turn it into a new operation. Same identity with different tool/parameters/fixed inputs is rejected. Summary arguments alone cannot prove equality.

Commit a document version and its receipt coherently. An identical replay returns the original result rather than inserting twice. A receipt saying “produced revision 4” may coexist with current head 5; report both as distinct facts. A new call with `expected_rev=3` after 4 exists is blocked by version checking, so it is a usability/reconciliation problem rather than proof of duplicate writing. Historical completion must not reset current pointers.

Optional `(base_revision, payload_hash)` deduplication must be scoped by document, operation kind, target, complete change, fixed referenced contents/assets, and base. Stable logical operation identity is separately scoped to its accepted response and batch; a content hash does not supply it. Identical table text inserted at different positions can be two valid operations. “Nearly identical” regeneration will not hash equally. Prefer preserving accepted calls and reconciling saved effects before asking the model to reconstruct an action. Optional exact deduplication does not establish a general intent recognizer.

topic: Full completion replay including graph updates
summary: The historical external-policy example replayed only `ToolMessage` after app policy 8 was saved but `Command(update={active_policy_rev:8})` was not checkpointed, leaving graph policy 7 active. That particular external policy/command mechanism was superseded by EVT-0878's compact Graph State policy and centralized settlement. The underlying completion lesson remains: preserve the committed domain result and any necessary supported state-update semantics, and reconstruct an equivalent completion without regressing newer state. Stable message identities and expected versions help avoid duplicates/regression. A design that persists only `Command.update` must explicitly limit supported forms; `goto`/`graph` cannot silently disappear. The final direct graph can concentrate state writes and reduce this machinery, while retaining the completion effects it actually supports.

topic: Stable message IDs do not resurrect safely
summary: `add_messages` replaces an existing same-ID entry; if compaction removed it, replay adds it again. Do not scan every successful receipt and re-inject historical messages, potentially orphaning ToolMessages. Let the runtime determine actual pending work, then reuse the corresponding receipt/completion when that work is invoked. Message identity is one aid, not a universal exactly-once or safe-history-replay guarantee.

Load session/checkpoint, reconcile effects, and continue the original state if usable. LangGraph has public state/history access and pending writes; the checked `create_agent` dispatched separate tools with `Send("tools", [tool_call])`. An unfinished superstep therefore does not prove every completed OCR must rerun. `StateSnapshot.tasks` contains `PregelTask` descriptions, not a guaranteed executable tool-call array. Use the runtime resume entry; when it actually invokes a tool, the wrapper checks its receipt. State snapshots serve diagnostics/status/checkpoint selection rather than a second scheduler.

Framework completion records are preferred; app results can cover the interval after an expensive tool finished but before its completion was durably recorded. Reuse checks source version, exact settings, and result completeness. This is useful even though “all tools always replay after a superstep crash” was false. It need not force every tiny operation through the same subprocess or blob machinery.

`returned_to_session_at` can be empty after the framework saved a result but before app timestamp update, or filled before framework persistence if ordered the other way. A hook seeing a result is not itself proof it survives a crash. Lack of a result in compacted active input is not evidence it was never delivered. Lazy acknowledgement can optimize common cases, backed by stable session/checkpoint identities and supported public-state reconciliation. Timestamps are observations, not joint transactions or proof of comprehension.

A named SQLite checkpointer does not determine durability: `sync`, `async`, and `exit` have different crash protection. A complete accepted response, each tool effect, and graph progress may be durable at different times. Recovery retains original persistent attempts/time budgets and does not re-publish a saved version. Final consolidation asks for explicit behavior at four boundaries: request saved, response accepted, tool committed, and graph recorded; arbitrary hard-crash or all-old-job recovery is not assumed.

topic: Working directories are not OS sandboxes
summary: Pointing cwd/environment at `script_runs/<operation_id>/out` does not prevent absolute-path or parent-directory writes. Trusted scripts execute with host-user permissions; directory separation is not an OS sandbox or automatic read-only enforcement. Full reconstruction does not silently change that security model. Any genuine restricted execution boundary needs a separately chosen mechanism, not a relabeled working folder.

`in_flight`/`spawning` can mean registered-before-launch, running, completed-before-receipt, or interrupted with partial output. The controller can crash after launch but before recording running, or after completion but before writing `_exit_status.json`. Nonzero exit can be an ordinary failure with reusable output. Even a zero exit and matching hashes do not prove scope/contract completion. Keep unknown states honest; logical operations and physical attempts are distinct, and each real subprocess attempt can retain process identity, working directory, logs, and outputs.

Windows `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` acts when the last job handle closes, for processes actually assigned to that job; handle inheritance, breakaway, assignment, and termination confirmation matter. `CREATE_SUSPENDED` then assignment has a crash gap; supported Windows can use `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` at process creation. A job may be destroyed before restart can query it. PID plus creation time helps identity but does not alone prove all descendants stopped. Other platforms require their own real lifecycle guarantees, not an assertion that process groups are equivalent. Apply this machinery only to actual subprocesses, not database note updates.

topic: Retry by effects not tool label
summary: Built-in OCR/rendering can be retryable when reading fixed inputs, writing only attempt-specific candidates, leaving formal versions unchanged, and ensuring old execution cannot continue modifying the same output. Being “built-in” does not prove those conditions. A host script without a final receipt is not blindly rerun, but evidence can still establish reusable completion or partial results. The agent may reconcile saved script, process state, outputs, and identifiable effects; only unresolved effects remain unknown or blocked. No routine human intervention is required for effects that can be safely reconciled within authorization.

topic: Separate inspect terminate and adopt intent
summary: Agents may inspect partial logs, malformed JSON, and damaged files to diagnose or repair; the whole directory need not validate first. Termination targets an identified attempt and is explicit, even if an interface combines steps. Salvaging one stable file does not imply stopping the entire attempt. Adoption selects a fixed consistent copy and validates that exact content. These internal responsibilities do not force a four-tool ritual on the agent.

A live writer can yield a torn copy. Holding a compatible read handle during snapshot acquisition is a possible Windows implementation. `GENERIC_WRITE` requests write access; `FILE_SHARE_WRITE` permits others' write access and does not mean that handle is writing. `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` means incompatible access/share modes, possibly an exclusive reader, not proof of an unknown descendant writing. Report snapshot unavailability and the observed error without inventing its cause.

topic: Decode versus completeness and independent salvage receipts
summary: Use mature full parsers/decoders; PNG endings/CRC or JPEG EOI alone do not replace decoding, and Pillow `verify()` differs from loading pixels. A syntactically valid JSON holding pages 1–30 is not successful completion of requested 1–100. Verify selected source/scope/content, record useful rescued ranges, and preserve the original failed/uncertain operation history.
